924f59c934: Genoryn Krypton Updates: Every Release and Change Since Launch
75680dc377: Everything that changed, since the first block.
f3a9370ca9: Every release of the wallet, the node and the miner, and every change to genoryn.io, newest first. Each release is signed with the project's post-quantum release key; the wallet checks that signature before it installs an update.
fa21553af2: No change to the rules of the chain: nodes and wallets on older versions keep working with this one. Coins, wallets and swaps in progress carry over.
96b06513c4: A new review of the whole system: the swaps with bitcoin, the node and its network, the desktop wallet, cryptography and the light client. Every finding it lists is fixed in this release; what was checked and what was fixed is at genoryn.io/audits.
39388b7eba: Light wallets check every block above the release checkpoint as a full node does: its proof of work, the difficulty the rule sets and its time. A node you add can no longer show your wallet blocks nobody worked for.
275dc354c0: Adding a wallet next to yours, switching between light and full mode and letting other nodes connect need the wallet's password.
0a1ed11104: Nodes check their peers' transactions outside their message loop and share their attention fairly, so one peer can no longer slow a node down for the others.
09e2473d72: Trade history in the wallet: every completed swap of the board, newest first, with charts, your own trades and a CSV export. It loads in parts, so it stays quick with millions of swaps; genoryn.io/trades shows the whole history.
f015ed5430: A sturdier market price (method 2): the shortest window with enough verified swaps, swaps far from the rest left out, limits per swap and per six hours, and a confidence from 0 to 100 with a status. The market page shows the depth of the board, and anyone can recompute the price with verifymarketprice in the wallet's console.
371652a658: Confirmations before every payment and swap: a bitcoin payment is checked first and shows the fee, the total and what stays; taking an offer or a Quick Swap shows what goes and what comes, the price against the market, the fees, the confirmations the seller waits for and what happens if the swap does not complete.
6464199212: Connect through Tor: an optional SOCKS5 proxy for all of the wallet's own connections, in Network, Connection mode.
fc5509847d: Swaps: the seller takes the bitcoin only with ten blocks of its lock left, and a claim waiting in a busy Bitcoin network is sent again every block with more fee. A seller whose buyer never claims the GNR gets it back when the lock ends.
4e6a2d1389: Nodes keep the whole trade history on disk and answer /v1/swap/history in pages.
eca3e8fcb8: Research: what a transaction still shows on chain, measured on mainnet, and why Sietch-style dummy outputs are not needed here: every transaction already has two inputs and two outputs.
7b08e2a095: A full security audit, and trading straight from your Bitcoin balance
46c1762aa6: A full audit of the whole system: the wallet, the swaps with bitcoin, Bitcoin keys and signing, the node and updates, consensus, the website and the forum. Every finding it lists is fixed in this release; what was checked and what was fixed is at genoryn.io/audits.
ee0fc52c8a: Swaps with bitcoin are safer at the step where a wallet decides that a Bitcoin transaction has done its job: a refund or a claim counts only once it is in a block, a dropped one is sent again, and a refund overtaken by the other side's claim still gets you your GNR.
1c196b4f28: Changing the nodes or the Bitcoin connection needs the wallet's password, and the 24-hour lock waits while your coins are in a swap.
23650d604a: Trade from your Bitcoin balance: take an offer and pay from the balance at once, publish a buy offer paid from it, and have what you sell paid into it. No address to type, no transfer each time.
558d0f1642: Swap, Market, Publish an offer and Your swaps are one Trade group, with your GNR and Bitcoin balances at the top of each page. Publishing an offer has a page of its own.
c567ce867f: Delete a wallet from this computer: with its password, never while a swap or an offer of it is open; keep an encrypted copy or erase it for good.
900476ad8b: A new Wallet page with the Bitcoin balance beside your GNR, a QR code to receive and a clearer send form; a console that looks like a terminal; a bigger About page with Genoryn Talks and the security audits; a start animation and a lock animation.
3f0a4ce343: The number of miners is no longer shown anywhere: it cannot be measured honestly. The hashrate and the difficulty are.
7780e4e25e: The totals on the History page no longer run into each other with long numbers.
b9b72a7543: genoryn.io: a Trade menu, the latest completed swaps on the home page, the security audits page, and a SHA-256 under every download button.
2812adee49: Swap and Market, each on a tab and a page of its own
b26f22eae5: The wallet has a Market tab of its own: the GNR price, the offer board and publishing an offer. The Swap tab keeps Quick Swap, your Bitcoin balance and your swaps.
eb00986fa1: A cleaner design for both: in Quick Swap what you pay stands above what you get, with a button between them that switches between buying and selling; the order book shows the market price between its sell and buy offers; the board's totals stand in one row, and its long explanation folds away.
aefc0b8ffa: genoryn.io/swap: Quick Swap on a page of its own, with the live price and what the board can swap right now. genoryn.io/market keeps the price, the order book, the price history and every completed swap.
ae09ee877a: Swaps that ended elsewhere close, and each wallet shows its own Bitcoin balance and miner
a659750031: A sale whose GNR came back through another copy of the wallet (a second computer, or the wallet restored from its phrase) no longer waits forever under Your swaps: it ends as refunded. The GNR was never lost; it was back in the wallet.
a63d1b42b8: Switching wallets shows the new wallet's Bitcoin balance and Quick Swap at once, not the last wallet's.
5577c70a27: The Mining tab says by name which wallet the miner pays, and offers to show it when you are looking at another wallet.
2026ba2257: Your own Quick Swap offers are not counted as ready to swap in your own wallet (you cannot swap with yourself); the wallet says they are listed for others.
0a664f15ec: The offer board's sell and buy tables no longer overlap
3694c6b35f: In the Swap tab, the sell and buy offers no longer run into each other: they stand side by side only where both fit, otherwise one under the other, and amounts of GNR are written shorter.
e52700949e: Quick Swap stays near the market price, and a burst of swaps cannot jump the price
f7680cb7f9: Price guard: Quick Swap takes no offer more than 20 % from the market price (10 % while the price is forming or the market is thin), and waits while the price is catching up with fast swaps. Offers further away stay on the board, marked far from the market, and can still be taken by hand.
b3cc7c5b83: The market price comes only from swaps whose bitcoin was found on the Bitcoin chain, of at least 0.001 BTC each, newer ones weighing more, and it moves at most 10 % an hour. Until there are three such swaps it is shown as forming.
0302dc97f5: Quick Swap offers follow the market price by default: at the market price or a margin above or below it, never past your limit, and taken off the board by themselves when the market reaches a trigger price you set.
699496c1be: The offer board shows how far each offer is from the market price, how much can be swapped within 2, 5, 10 and 20 % of it, and the bitcoin buyers have deposited.
f48f4d7e98: "Ready to buy" counts only what Quick Swap can really swap near the market price, not offers at many times the price.
48371464ec: More of the wallet's messages are translated (Quick Swap, offers, passwords, updates).
7ffc684733: The wallet and genoryn.io in ten languages, Hive OS for mining rigs
1d8deceb3a: No change to the rules of the chain: nodes and wallets on older versions keep working with this one.
e80367e84e: The wallet and genoryn.io in ten languages: English, Deutsch, Français, Español, Português, Русский, Türkçe, 简体中文, 日本語 and 한국어. Choose the wallet's language in the new Settings tab. Recovery-phrase words, addresses and swap codes are never translated. The translations are machine translations for now; corrections are welcome.
4ca03b70e7: Hive OS: a custom miner package for GPU rigs that checks the miner's SHA-256 checksum before it starts, with a setup guide. Reports from real rigs are welcome.
91b188da05: Check your miner on genoryn.io/mining: enter your address to see whether its shares are reaching the network, an estimate of its hashrate, the rewards accruing and the next payout.
8dda244e72: The wallet's Mining tab shows rejected shares, the last share, how long the miner has been running and its average hashrate over 24 hours.
a509b61a9d: The miner accepts the short address (gnrs1…) as its payout address and checks it against the full address the node returns; its JSON output includes its version, uptime and the time of the last share.
0fb14e1df7: Display and connection settings moved from the Network tab to the new Settings tab.
551e72462a: About one swap in 256 could not start ("lock commitment mismatch"); such swaps now start like any other. No coins were at risk: nothing was locked.
242bc0aea1: On phones, the Network tab no longer scrolls sideways.
347e003a83: Guides for miners: how native rewards work and are calculated, mining compared with pools, security and a FAQ. A contributing guide for translations and mining integrations, a security policy with response times, and a roadmap.
eb537b2ead: Quick Swap: buy or sell any amount of GNR in one click
61d77a492d: Quick Swap, at the top of the Swap tab: say how much you want to buy or sell, in dollars, bitcoin or GNR, and press one button. The wallet finds the best prices on the board and swaps exactly that amount across up to three offers whose makers are online, each part its own atomic swap. The seller's GNR is still locked on chain before any bitcoin moves.
c1bb9c5dda: A part that cannot start (someone else took that offer a moment earlier, or its maker went offline) is replaced by another offer, never at a worse price than the one you accepted.
6373a6bcaf: Your Bitcoin balance for Quick Swap: an address of the wallet's own, from your 24 words. Buying pays from it at once, selling is paid into it, and you can send bitcoin out of it at any time.
b8354fafb5: Quick Swap offers: tick Quick Swap when you publish, and anyone can buy (or sell you) any part of the offer, from its smallest part up to all of it, at your price. It is listed as up to three lots so several people can swap at once, and after a part the rest goes back on the board by itself.
c44b8f8027: The board adds up what a buyer's deposit is promised to across all sellers, so bitcoin for one swap cannot have the GNR of many sellers locked at once.
d5bfddc125: Buying at the market price is clearer: you set only the bitcoin you spend, and the wallet shows the GNR you get now and the least you get at your limit.
4669eed835: genoryn.io/market shows Quick Swap live: what can be bought and sold right now, how many parts are swapping, and what an amount would get.
ef59c4ca37: No change to the rules of the chain: nodes and wallets on older versions keep working with this one, and see Quick Swap offers as ordinary offers.
cc204b67ba: Old 24-word recovery phrases restore as people wrote them down
7d8eaf369a: A recovery phrase written down with the positions the wallets show next to each word (1. abandon, 2. ability …) restores as it is, one word per line or on one line, with or without commas. Before, the positions made the wallet expect a numbered Krypton phrase and refuse it.
c9c2d6eba5: A phrase of 24 words without numbers, as Genoryn Mainnet 1.0 and other wallets made them, restores as before, and the wallet now says what that means: it finds what those words received on Genoryn Krypton. Mainnet 1.0 was a separate chain and its coins are not on Krypton.
60a1515160: When a phrase mixes words with and without numbers, the wallet explains the two kinds of phrase instead of only asking for a number.
167f836341: No change to the rules of the chain or to swaps.
211629b576: A console in the wallet, offers that follow the market, a market price that rests on bitcoin really paid
82b1474e43: The wallet has a Console: type a command and read the answer, as in Bitcoin's wallet. It completes commands as you type, keeps earlier lines, and <0/> lists everything: blocks, transactions, peers, addresses, the supply, your balance. It only reads: no command can send GNR or show a recovery phrase or a key.
5fdf695ce3: History links straight to the explorer: View opens a payment's transaction on genoryn.io, Block the block that holds it. The explorer never shows an amount or who paid whom.
aa74847c3d: An offer can follow the market price. A sell offer keeps its GNR and a buy offer its bitcoin; what is asked for it moves with the market, at most every ten minutes and by at most 5 % at a time. It never passes the limit you set: a sell offer never asks less, a buy offer never pays more.
d09c784142: The market price now rests on bitcoin found on the Bitcoin chain. A swap's report names its bitcoin contract and is signed by one of the swap's two wallets; the board looks the payment up. With three such swaps the price is their volume-weighted median, and no single swap weighs more than a fifth. Reports nobody proved weigh nothing then.
bc70ec4f7a: genoryn.io has a guide to running a full node on Linux, Windows and macOS, pages on validation, privacy, requirements, the user interface and network support, and pages for getting help, reporting bugs and contributing.
b038b66866: The Linux service script works from the release packages (its line endings broke it before), finds the programs the package installed, and no longer switches a firewall on that was off.
fa92a4523e: Offers only for buyers whose bitcoin is ready, faster swaps, one wallet on two computers
634cc1865d: A sell offer can be for buyers whose bitcoin is already deposited (the default). The seller's wallet checks on the Bitcoin chain that the bitcoin is waiting before it locks any GNR, so nobody can take the offer and leave the GNR locked unpaid.
f8503c6265: For other buyers a wallet locks GNR for at most two at a time who have not paid.
5bc710a115: Fewer confirmations before a buyer pays, by the size of the payment: 3 GNR blocks up to 0.001 BTC, 6 up to 0.01 BTC, 15 up to 0.1 BTC, 30 above. A small swap now starts in about three minutes instead of fifteen.
a5c7dba041: Shorter locks when both wallets are on this version: GNR of a swap nobody pays comes back after about 21 hours instead of 32, and the bitcoin lock is about 3 hours instead of 6.
075b09574d: One wallet on two computers: each shows the swaps the other runs, with their progress, and can carry a swap on if the other computer is switched off or lost.
8e93f1a80f: Updates install by themselves while no swap is running, unless you turn that off under About. Linux nodes update with one command.
3bb54c5276: A sell offer commits its GNR for a week; nothing waits without saying why
fe168ca5b5: Publishing a sell offer commits its GNR for 7 days. Within that time it can be sold or put into another sell offer at once, but not sent, also after you cancel or the offer runs its time. The wallet shows this before you publish.
883950798d: A seller whose buyer did not pay sees the block at which the GNR returns and about how many hours that is. The GNR is safe; nobody can open such a lock sooner, and the wallet takes it back by itself.
0be698409d: Taking a buy offer that the other wallet does not answer is shown while it waits and ends by itself after ten minutes. Before, it stayed open without being shown.
1e1521391c: A swap that ran out ends even while the Bitcoin server cannot be reached, and a swap that waits for that server says so.
587fe8446d: A seller whose bitcoin claim lost to the buyer's refund takes the GNR back at its refund block.
a1b74f9eff: Buy offers with the bitcoin deposited: the swap completes by itself
354c3c60f5: A buy offer is now paid in advance, to an address of the buyer's own wallet. The wallet shows the address and the amount, and publishes the offer by itself once the bitcoin has one confirmation.
d0323717f4: The offer board checks on the Bitcoin chain that the bitcoin is there and marks the offer with a ✓. It keeps the address to itself.
ee5acd4889: When a seller takes the offer, the buyer does nothing: once the seller's GNR is locked and confirmed, the buyer's wallet pays the swap contract from the deposit, exactly the agreed amount, and then claims the GNR.
123da974d0: Buying from a sell offer works the same way: pay once, to an address of your wallet, and the swap starts and completes by itself. The seller's GNR is locked only once the buyer's bitcoin is there.
558f44c4a3: If the offer is cancelled, nobody sells, or the offer you wanted is gone, the wallet sends the bitcoin back to your address. What was set aside for the network fee and not used comes back too.
0362d4fa3f: A wallet restored from its 24 words finds bitcoin left from buy offers again: Swap, Bitcoin connection.
bfe189c248: The same wallet open on two computers: the second one now shows GNR that the first has locked in a swap, with the block at which it returns, and takes it back itself if the first is gone when the lock ends. Offers of two copies no longer share a mailbox.
52438b8d7d: A seller whose buyer cancelled or did not pay is told so, with the block at which the GNR returns.
444f521e90: A sell offer is listed only after its GNR is set aside in a note of its own and the offer board has checked a zero-knowledge proof that it is there. Nobody can offer GNR they do not have.
162544ecb1: The board takes an offer down the moment the GNR behind it moves. The same GNR cannot back two offers, or an offer and a swap in progress.
ea444e7209: The wallet shows the rules before you publish. GNR of a cancelled sell offer is free again 24 hours later (or when the offer would have ended, if sooner) and can go into a new offer at once.
631831ea73: A take locks exactly the GNR that was set aside, so a seller's lock no longer waits for notes to be merged.
d9c05ecedd: GNR set aside for an offer that ran its time, or whose swap ended, is free again by itself, also while the board cannot be reached.
577732afaf: A swap accepted just before the wallet was closed carries on when the wallet starts again.
aea01ad4d9: The offer board was cleared when it switched to these rules: every offer on it now follows them.
